author: Howard Pyle
title: Pepper & Salt; or, Seasoning for Young Folk
edition: Text used: the Project Gutenberg 15664 plain-text transcription (https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/15664.txt.utf-8) of the E. M. Hale and Company, Eau Claire, Wisconsin, special edition "published by arrangement with the publishers of the regular edition, Harper & Brothers". In that plain-text file the transcribed title-page block carries the line "1885, reissued 1913."; the HTML transcription of the same Hale title page (https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/15664/pg15664-images.html) prints no date. That line is therefore not treated as a printed date of the exemplar: the Hale printing is undated and its relation to any one print copy is not asserted. Every selected passage was collated in full against a dated Harper & Brothers, New York, printing (https://archive.org/details/peppersaltorseas00pyle2): its title page (scan leaf n8) reads MCMVI (1906), and its verso (leaf n9) reads “Entered according to Act of Congress, in the year 1885, by Harper & Brothers.” publicationYear records that 1906 witness. Six transcription errors in the Gutenberg text are corrected to its page images and nothing else is changed: "he is wandering" to "he's wandering" (Three Fortunes); "The he left" to "Then he left", "said that done" to "said than done", and "If we had two wishes" to "If we had had two wishes" (Ye Two Wishes); "This man" to "That man" (A Verse with a Moral but No Name); "dairies" to "daisies" (The Force of Need); and the printed "Jame- / -s;" line break is restored in Superficial Culture. The nine poems are supplied from the plain-text file; the prose preface is supplied from the HTML transcription of the same Gutenberg edition, which renders the printed dashes as em dashes where the plain text uses double hyphens. Poems retain Gutenberg ASCII punctuation, emphasis underscores and indentation; prose wrapping is reflowed; illustrations, captions and signatures are excluded. Library text: the whole plain-text file (textUrl) with the six corrections and the restored line break above applied, except the prose preface, which follows the HTML transcription as the selected excerpt does; the stories therefore keep the plain text's double hyphens while the preface has em dashes. On 2026-11-18 the further passages read by Grade 2 calendar readings (The Skillful Huntsman, blocks 11–99; Venturesome Boldness, 204–207; A Victim to Science, 268–270; Play & Earnest, 272–274; The Accident of Birth, 276–280) were collated in full against the same 1906 witness, the typeset prose word by word against its OCR text (https://archive.org/download/peppersaltorseas00pyle2/peppersaltorseas00pyle2_djvu.txt) and the hand-lettered verses word by word against the page images themselves, every difference decided on the page images; twenty-five readings of the witness are adopted, changing six readings: "woodpile" to "wood-pile" (twice, printed mid-line) and "Oh, if that was all" to "Oh! if that was all" (The Skillful Huntsman); "going Sir?" to "going, sir?", "In our house" to "In our house,", "men that I" to "men than I", "In armor bright" to "In armor bright,", "said he;" to "said he" and "A little man." to "A little man," (Venturesome Boldness); "walked and talked" to "walked, and talked", "interesting case," to "interesting case;" and "th's, my pills are better much." to "th's; my pills are better, much." (A Victim to Science); "breeze," to "breeze:" and "crowns" to "crown;" (Play & Earnest); and ten "the" or "The" to the lettered "ye" or "Ye" (The Accident of Birth: unto ye Saint, to be ye King, At last ye Saint ye King's, to ye same, Ye same words, bear ye gift, Ye cobbler, so ye baby, tell ye difference), the convention A Victim to Science already keeps. On 2026-11-18 two further stories read by Grade 2 calendar readings (Hans Hecklemann's Luck, blocks 389–455, and Farmer Griggs's Boggart, 488–532) were collated in full against the same 1906 witness, the typeset prose word by word against its OCR text and every page also read on its image, since the OCR comparison does not show apostrophe spacing; twenty-four readings of the witness are adopted, and no earlier reading cited those blocks: "his luck about with him" to "their luck about with them", "or not" to "or no", "that, either" to "that either", "his finger" to "their finger", "bargain, after all" to "bargain after all", "good luck, after all" to "good luck after all", and the moral's wrapped line "cabbages--with / money." restored to its one printed line (Hans Hecklemann's Luck); "latticed windows" to "latticed-windows" (printed mid-line), "Did'ee", "Look'ee" (twice), "will'ee" and "Dost'ee" to the printed "Did 'ee", "Look 'ee", "will 'ee" and "Dost 'ee", "o'mine" to "o' mine", "thee"; and" to "thee;" and", "me, then?" to "me then?", "know," said" to "know" said", "lettin' th'" to "letten' th'", "a-packing" to "a packing", "find a new home" to "find them a new home", "Oft" to "Off", "night or day" to "night nor day", "topsy-turvy" to "topsy-turvey" and "clad in all" to "clad all in" (Farmer Griggs's Boggart).

rights.basis: The collated witness is the Harper & Brothers printing dated MCMVI (1906) on its title page; its verso records the 1885 copyright entry of this original English text. Both dates are before 1931, so the text is public domain in the United States as of 2026. Project Gutenberg 15664 independently states public domain in the USA. Every selected passage was checked against the dated witness.

acquisition.method: Downloaded two files from the aleph.pglaf.org mirror, in this order: (1) the Project Gutenberg plain text https://aleph.pglaf.org/cache/epub/15664/pg15664.txt (the same file as textUrl; SHA-256 19ada1b4575f5e80ea491bc19c2052dfa3769f3bf3c5bb96c385dbf0cf653121), and (2) the HTML transcription of the same edition https://aleph.pglaf.org/cache/epub/15664/pg15664-images.html (SHA-256 3040c4d0bd9f10080d67de39cce40a3de0b47da80d0d0bce2e9b0f02dbbf6ceb), used only for the preface; downloadUrl names the first file and downloadSha256 is the SHA-256 of the two files concatenated in that order. The plain text was converted with a scratch script: CR line ends removed; text between blank lines forms blocks; uppercase title lines (and the mixed-case title "Ye song of ye foolish old woman.", the "(Ye first opinion)"/"(Ye second opinion)" labels and the part number "II") become headings; within poems every block is a stanza keeping its lines and leading-space indentation, and within the seven prose tales a block is a stanza only when a line is indented or every line is shorter than 60 characters, otherwise a paragraph with its lines joined by single spaces; _underscore_ emphasis and double hyphens kept. Omitted: the Project Gutenberg header, footer and licence, the title page and Hale imprint, the contents and list of illustrations, every [Illustration] marker with its transcriber's description of the picture, and the artist's signatures under the pictures ("H. Pyle", "HP", "H.P. MDCCCLXXXIII" and the like). The PREFACE heading comes from the plain text; its eight paragraphs come from the HTML file (2), converted with the scratch HTML parser used for the other works. Corrections applied as single-occurrence replacements: “he is wandering to this day” to “he's wandering to this day”; “The he left” to “Then he left”; “said that done” to “said than done”; “If we had two wishes” to “If we had had two wishes”; “This man of great renown” to “That man of great renown”; “nodding dairies” to “nodding daisies”; “Was James; /   and whose” to “Was Jame- /   -s; and whose”. Further corrections to the 1906 witness (2026-11-18), as single-occurrence replacements within their blocks: “back of the woodpile” to “back of the wood-pile” (twice, in two paragraphs); “Oh, if that was all” to “Oh! if that was all”; “going Sir?” to “going, sir?”; “In our house” to “In our house,”; “greater men that I” to “greater men than I”; “In armor bright” to “In armor bright,”; “draw," said he;” to “draw," said he”; “A little man.” to “A little man,”; “as they walked and talked” to “as they walked, and talked”; “an interesting case,” to “an interesting case;”; “difficult as th's, my pills are better much.” to “difficult as th's; my pills are better, much.”; “called to the breeze,” to “called to the breeze:”; “from its crowns” to “from its crown;”; “unto the Saint”, “to be the King”, “At last the Saint the King's”, “bear him to the same”, “The same words”, “bear the gift to Fritz / The cobbler”, “And so the baby” and “tell the difference” to the same with “ye”/“Ye”. Further emendations to the 1906 witness (2026-11-18), each a single-occurrence replacement within its block: in Hans Hecklemann's Luck "everybody carries his luck about with him;" to "everybody carries their luck about with them;", "whether or not it might" to "whether or no it might", "such luck as that, either!" to "such luck as that either!", "with his finger and thumb" to "with their finger and thumb", "bargain, after all." to "bargain after all.", in the moral "cabbages--with" and "money." joined on one line and "good luck, after all!" to "good luck after all!"; in Farmer Griggs's Boggart "latticed windows" to "latticed-windows", "Did'ee hear" to "Did 'ee hear", "Look'ee now" to "Look 'ee now", "o'mine" to "o' mine", "o' thee"; and" to "o' thee;" and", "will'ee do me, then?" to "will 'ee do me then?", "know," said" to "know" said", "lettin' th'" to "letten' th'", "a-packing" to "a packing", "Look'ee, now" to "Look 'ee, now", "Dost'ee" to "Dost 'ee", "find a new home" to "find them a new home", "Oft they trudged" to "Off they trudged", "night or day" to "night nor day", "topsy-turvy" to "topsy-turvey" and "clad in all his" to "clad all in his".
